posts.author: aLostSolo
posts.body:
Hello everyone,
I wanted to test my RPG Maker MV game on my Android device - Google Pixel 6 and I've encountered very disturbing lag issues.
Now I know this has been addressed on multiple threads as I've read through each and every one of them to try and solve multiple issues I've encountered and all were resolved except for the lag.
I noticed the most noticeable lag occurs when animations are played - Especially during battles.
There is also some small lag when interacting with events that open a message box.
To me, this makes the game pretty much unplayable.
Details about everything I've tried (And haven't tried for a reason):
I have approximately 1.2GB of assets which consist of audio and images. I know this is a lot and I have plans to minimize it but I doubt it'll be less than ~800MB as my game is quite big with a lot of content.
I saw
this thread
where
@Milennin
mentioned having the same issues and was recommended to reduce the assets sizes, however that
did not
solve the issue after reducing ~70-80% files size.
That's the main reason I haven't tried it, though I do plan to do it anyways for optimization reasons.
I have used
this guide
by
@TehGuy
(Combined with
this guide
),
without the Google Play Store part
, to move all my assets to an OBB file and that seems to have worked as my APK is ~7MB in size and the game works but I did not see any improvement in the lag.
All parallel process events have a small "wait 5 frames" to improve performance on all maps.
I have a lot of Yanfly's scrips that have some optimizations and have written a lot of code myself and did the best to optimize my own code as well.
I know a lot of assets are already cached either by the latest updates to RPG Maker MV or the optimizations done by Yanfly's core plugin so I'm not sure if adding even more caching would help, especially when I've read there's still a limit to the amount of memory allocated to the app even in a relatively strong device as the Pixel 6.
As a side note, I've solved all other issues like Iconset size being 4096px in height resulting in black boxes for icons and setting `PRECISION_FRAGMENT` to "highp" to solve the tilesets black lines issue.
Another thing worth mentioning is that I run my game on a very strong PC and relatively weak laptop on battery and I have never encountered anything like the lag I experience.
I'd like to know if anyone has any suggestions on how to solve this as I was really hoping to release it not only for PC...
Thanks in advance for you patience and help.

are you using default mapping or is there anything added to the mapping process (Parallax, doodads, external editor,...)
aLostSolo said:
I ran much more demanding games on it and they worked well
Click to expand...
doesn't really matter as those other cames are most likely compiled for Android.
RPG Maker is NOT a compiler engine, but an interpreter based engine - actually it's doubly interpreted in case of event code, and that costs a lot of performance.
Which is the reason why you have to keep the limitations of android in mind even before beginning to develop the game, or you end up looking for where the lag comes from.

posts.author: SangHendrix
posts.body:
Experienced RPG Maker Android dev here. You'd be surprised by how unoptimized most plugins on the forum are (for mobile). Large maps alone don't affect performance as you think they would.
Avoid big sprite files. Mobile can't handle a large sprite sheet. Something above 500x500 that is constantly being called would already give massive lag. Just don't use the default RPG Maker spritesheet animation system lol.

So for example, if you have a 1024x1024 animation spritesheet file running constantly or a lot of animation is being played using said file, it'll overload your mobile device due to it having to load the file and run it again and again, making the fps drops. RPG Maker is extremely bad for mobile development. Barely anyone put their game on mobile so the subject was not widely discussed. I had to create my own animation system using singular frames instead of spritesheets for this matter alone, lol.
Here are my tips for a good performance on mobile:
- Don't use a large spritesheet file, something above 1000x1000 is already large (depending on how powerful the device is). LOTS of people use low-end phones so probably 500x500 is already too big.
- Compressing your file size also helps a little. An extra 2 - 3 framerate is better than nothing.
- Check all your plugins. Optimize any plugins that have a function to update along with the game every frame, these plugins contributed A LOT to your performance failure. They're basically like when you're running parallel events but not all tasks are lightweight. Optimize them by yourself (cuz devs are probably retired).
